Australia’s richest person, Gina Rinehart, lobbied for controversial plans to host 2032 Olympic rowing events on the Fitzroy River at Rockhampton, documents released by the Queensland government show.

title: Gina Rinehart lobbied for controversial plan to move 2032 Olympic rowing to crocodile-inhabited river

author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
description:
Prime minister to highlight investment in communities as he launches next phase of nuclear submarine replacement

Andy Burnham will place the renewal of Trident at the heart of his vision of a reindustrialised Britain on Thursday when he travels to Barrow-in-Furness to launch the next phase of the nuclear submarine replacement programme.

The new prime minister intends to emphasise that defence spending on projects such as the £31bn Dreadnought-class boats built in the Cumbrian town is a case study of taxpayer investment revitalising communities around the UK.

Continue reading...
title: Trident renewal central to defence spending, says Andy Burnham

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Government’s special envoy returns to the witness box again today; three victims found in burned-out house in Wiley Park. Follow updates live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Three people have died following a house fire in Sydney’s south-west last night, NSW police said.

Emergency services were called to a home on Cornelia Street, Wiley Park, at about 9.45pm following reports of a fire.

This result is encouraging, as are improvements in eight other targets including employment and education.

However, it is very concerning that we are still seeing outcomes worsening for early childhood development, children in out-of-home care, incarceration rates and suicide.
title: Australia news live: Jillian Segal returns to antisemitism royal commission; three dead in Sydney house fire

author: Sam Levine in New York City
description:
Republican John Cornyn says he will not back nomination without written confirmation $1.8bn slush fund is dead

Todd Blanche’s hopes of becoming US attorney general seemed to be in jeopardy on Wednesday after the Department of Justice did not provide written assurances to a key Republican senator that a $1.8bn slush fund was dead.

The US Senate judiciary committee will hold a vote on Thursday on whether to advance Blanche’s nomination.

Continue reading...
title: Todd Blanche’s US attorney general prospects in question as vote looms

author: Dan Milmo and Vikram Dodd
description:
Details of parents and staff, including email addresses and phone numbers, are among data taken by cybercriminals

The Department for Education and a police database have been targeted by a cyber-attack, exposing more than 740,000 pieces of data.

Details of government officials, senior school leaders, university staff, police officers and members of the public have been taken by hackers.

Continue reading...
title: Hackers steal sensitive data from Department for Education and police

author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
description:
Rightwing media hostility helped sink his reform plans in 2010, but the new PM’s passionate speech suggests there is now clear political will for change

For campaigners perpetually disappointed by the failure of England’s political classes to fix England’s creaking adult social care system, the fear was that Andy Burnham’s long-trailed speech on Wednesday would be less Brave New World, more Groundhog Day.

Burnham acknowledged he had been here before. Back in 2010, as health and social care secretary, he unveiled extensive proposals to overhaul social care, only for them to collapse amid rightwing media hostility and furious political rows about “death taxes”.

Continue reading...
title: Brave New World or Groundhog Day? Burnham revisits old ground in speech on social care

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
Rates remain unchanged for fifth time since December as tenuous Iran peace deal pushes energy prices up again

The US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday, leaving rates unchanged for the fifth time since December despite Donald Trump’s renewed calls to lower rates.

Cooler inflation data published earlier this month eased expectations for an imminent rate hike. But the tenuous peace deal between the US and Iran have made energy prices creep up again, strengthening the case for an increase. The Fed’s federal open market committee voted 9-3 to maintain rates, with three dissenting members who preferred to raise the rate by a quarter-percentage point.

Continue reading...
title: Fed holds interest rates steady despite Trump’s renewed calls to lower them

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Planned overhaul forms part of president’s broader pattern of directing changes in Washington after arch and ballroom

Donald Trump is due to announce a $22bn plan to rebuild Washington’s Dulles international airport on Wednesday after the US president personally weighed in on the design of the capital’s main international gateway.

A White House official confirmed an announcement would be made, after CBS News reported that Trump had scrutinized 3D models from contractors competing to carry out the overhaul at the White House, and offered proposed changes.

Continue reading...
title: Trump to announce $22bn plan to rebuild Dulles international airport

author: Associated Press
description:
Lawyers for Massachusetts mother say she was in throes of postpartum psychosis amid January 2023 tragedy

More than three years after a Massachusetts mother strangled her three young children, her former husband described returning home to the aftermath and a jury listened on Wednesday to his frantic 911 call, as her lawyers seek to prove she was in the grip of post-pregnancy psychosis.

Lindsay Clancy, 35, admits she killed her children in January 2023 while her then husband was ⁠on an errand away from their home in the Boston suburb of Duxbury. Her attorney says she was driven by postpartum mental illness and a jury cannot find she intentionally murdered the children.

Continue reading...
title: Lindsay Clancy’s ex-husband testifies about day she killed their three children

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Transport for London claims polluting diesel vehicles had been able to enter clean air zone without having to pay

Transport for London is pursuing a potential £1bn legal action against car manufacturers over vehicles that it argues should not have been allowed to drive freely in the capital’s clean-air zone.

The high court heard that TfL was making allegations of “fraud and negligence” against manufacturers including Stellantis, Jaguar Land Rover, BMW and Nissan over their vehicles’ levels of diesel emissions.

Continue reading...
title: TfL brings case worth up to £1bn against carmakers over Ulez compliance

author: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent
description:
V&A Storehouse dispute centres on toilet and hydration breaks as employees across V&A in London also vote to strike in wider action

Staff at the V&A’s Storehouse site in east London have voted overwhelmingly to strike in a dispute over what they say are inadequate toilet and hydration breaks.

They will join staff across V&A sites in London who on Wednesday also voted to strike in a wider dispute over pay, working conditions, and the museum having declined to seek living wage accreditation.

Continue reading...
title: Staff at newest V&A site in London vote overwhelmingly for strike action

author: Sam Levine in New York
description:
Comey’s lawyers say Secret Service tracked him and investigators turned to AI and a mafia killer to bolster case

Lawyers for former FBI director James Comey alleged on Tuesday that US Secret Service agents illegally surveilled Comey, Donald Trump requested regular updates into the investigation, and law enforcement turned to ChatGPT and a known mafia killer as they scrambled to find justification for criminally charging Comey for posting a picture of seashells that spelled out “8647”.

The claims were laid out in a motion to dismiss a criminal case the US Department of Justice filed against Comey in April, in which it said the post by Comey – whom Trump fired in his first term – was a threat on the US president’s
title: Comey alleges Trump pushed prosecution over ‘8647’ seashell post

author: Petra Stock
description:
Exclusive: Scientists say about 5,000 fewer southern bent-wing bats have been recorded at a key maternity site for the species

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A sudden decline in critically endangered bats is troubling experts, who recorded about 5,000 fewer southern bent-wing bats than usual at Naracoorte’s “bat cave” this summer.

These tiny russet-toned microbats roost in caves and forage for insects over long distances across south-west Victoria and south-east South Australia.
title: The population of an endangered Australian bat suddenly dropped by up to 16%. No one knows why

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Some companies reportedly using leaderboards for employees who used the most AI in their work

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Software firm Atlassian has sought to tighten tracking of its staff’s AI spending by introducing “wallets” with monthly caps of up $2,000 for each employee, amid an explosion in costs at other tech companies.

The move by Atlassian, which recently cited AI as part of the reason behind cutting 1,600 staff, bucks the trend of others in the tech sector who encouraged employees to use as much of the technology as possible, dubbed “tokenmaxxing”. Some companies have
title: Atlassian tightens tracking of staff AI use as other technology firms encourage ‘tokenmaxxing’

author: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent
description:
Clean Energy Council calls for a national, legislated scheme to funnel benefits of hosting renewables projects back to local councils

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Organised campaigns against wind and solar energy have proved “extremely effective” in undermining community support for renewable energy but enthusiasm for electric vehicles has jumped following Donald Trump’s attack on Iran, according to a detailed snapshot of Australian attitudes to the clean energy transition.

The survey found levels of “deep support” for clean technologies were highest for home batteries and rooftop solar and also improving for major infrastructure projects such as transmission lines, which have been a target for critics of renewables.
title: Australians value batteries and EVs, but renewables industry must earn trust of regions, summit told

author: Donna Lu
description:
Authorities say local transmission of H5 bird flu virus among South Australian birds signals ‘shift in the situation’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia has entered a new phase in dealing with the incursion of deadly H5N1 bird flu, with authorities confirming on Wednesday that local transmission of the highly virulent strain had taken place.

“We have had what is suggestive of local transmission for the first time,” Julie Collins, the federal minister for agriculture, fisheries and forestry, said on Wednesday afternoon, after 11 new suspected detections were reported in South Australian birds.
title: Bird flu is spreading locally and Australia faces more wildlife deaths. How bad could it get?

author: Anne Davies
description:
Dirt files are always damaging – not least those originating in the secretive rightwing Reformers sub-faction of the party

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

From time to time, dirt files – crudely known as shit sheets – flutter around the corridors of power in state and federal parliaments.

They can be enormously damaging even if never published. While there might be speculation as to their origin, rarely is there confirmation – especially if the dirt file emanates from your own side.

Continue reading...
title: Icac hits paydirt as Reformers’ ‘shit sheets’ are given a very public airing

author: Ajit Niranjan and Jennifer Rankin
description:
Comments by Pedro Sánchez come as extreme heat renews pressure on firefighters tackling blazes across southern Europe

  • Europe live – latest updates

The next 12 hours will be “decisive” for a large wildfire burning near Madrid, the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has said, as extreme heat renews pressure on firefighters racing to control blazes across southern Europe.

Temperatures pushed higher by climate breakdown are forecast to reach 39C on Wednesday in Bordeaux, where firefighters have kept a monster blaze in nearby pine forests from reaching the suburbs, and 37C in Madrid, west of which Spain’s largest wildfire on record is burning.
title: Next 12 hours ‘decisive’ for wildfire near Madrid, says Spanish PM

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Lightning kills a New Jersey man as rescues, power outages and travel disruption hit region

Bands of deadly, extreme weather including torrential rain and high winds sparked flash flooding and tornado warnings in several north eastern US states Tuesday night and into Wednesday, knocking out power for hundreds of thousands of people and playing havoc with travel.

A 32-year-old man was killed on Tuesday afternoon in a lightning strike in Monroe township, New Jersey, authorities said.

Continue reading...
title: Flash floods and storms batter north-east US as deadly weather threatens millions

author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
description:
Introducing legislation would be ‘very challenging’ until care system improved, PM says

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham has said the assisted dying debate needs to wait until palliative care and social care are fixed, as he set out his path to resolving one of the most intractable problems in British politics.

The prime minister said he was not opposed to having the debate on assisted dying, but told reporters it would be “very challenging” to introduce the controversial legislation until the care system was in a better place.

Continue reading...
title: Assisted dying debate should come after end-of-life care reform, says Burnham

description:
Musa Ahmed was being treated in intensive care in London hospital after being pulled from West Mersea sea

A seven-year-old boy has died a week after an incident off the Essex coast in which his teenage cousin and her mother died as they tried to rescue him.

Musa Ahmed was being treated for life-threatening injuries after being pulled from the sea near West Mersea beach on 22 July.

Continue reading...
title: Boy, seven, dies after Essex coast incident that killed cousin and aunt

author: Pippa Neill
description:
Environment Agency names seven regions affected by unusually hot and dry weather and shortage of water

Half of England is officially in drought, with July set to be the driest on record after winter floods, the Environment Agency has said.

The “flash drought” developed quickly because of unusually low rainfall and high temperatures.

Continue reading...
title: Half of England officially in ‘exceptionally serious’ drought

author: Helena Horton
description:
Exclusive: British garden staple becomes plant most frequently reported as suffering in heat, charity reports

With their lush foliage and blooms that turn pink, purple or blue depending on the soil, hydrangeas are a firm favourite in Britain.

The shrubs bloom throughout summer and have historically thrived in the mild, damp British climate. But hotter summers and heatwaves such as the one hitting parts of England this week are putting the flower at risk in the south of the country, the Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) has said.

Continue reading...
title: Hotter summers may force RHS to move hydrangeas to north of England

description:
Districts are reducing routes and exploring new ways to get students to class as transportation costs climb

Education officials across the United States are increasingly facing a fundamental challenge: how do they ensure that school students can actually get to their classrooms?

The bright yellow school bus might be a visual icon of US education famous around the world, but in reality it is becoming harder for districts to steer.

Continue reading...
title: US schools are struggling to keep the yellow bus running amid shortages and cuts

Veteran medical adviser likely to face questions over disputed ‘lab leak’ theory in investigation seen by scientists as ‘vilification and harassment’ of 85-year-old

Scientists have scrambled to Anthony Fauci’s defense ahead of the unusual hearing, the second time the longtime National Institutes of Health scientist has been before Congress to discuss pandemic origins since leaving the government in 2022.

While the Covid-19 pandemic introduced him to millions of Americans, he talked the nation through numerous outbreaks over decades, including HIV, Ebola and the 2001 anthrax attacks, while advising seven presidents.
title: Fauci to face Republican questions over Covid pandemic origins – US politics live

description:
US military says it intercepted all Iranian missiles, as fighting threatens to resume. Plus, how Armenians seek to breathe more easily by heading underground

Good morning.

The US military has claimed it knocked down an Iranian missile barrage and worked with Saudi forces to strike sites in Iraq that Tehran-backed militias have used to launch attacks in recent days. In what Washington cast ⁠as “an attempted surprise ⁠attack” by Tehran, Iran had launched ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East, shattering a brief pause in fighting. description:
Rise to £1.1bn in first six months of year for bakery chain largely down to opening of new stores

Iced matcha lattes and a bigger range of salads and chicken rolls helped Greggs to boost its sales during the string of summer heatwaves, as the bakery chain continues to expand across the UK.

Total sales at Britain’s biggest fast food business rose to £1.1bn for the first six months of the year, 7.2% higher than the same period a year earlier.

Continue reading...
title: Greggs sales jump as iced matcha lattes and chicken rolls become heatwave hits

Rescuers pulling people from the wreckage in southern Japan in a haunting repeat of disaster that struck 10 years ago

description:
PM will not discuss details but will focus on need to find ‘common ground’ and to build political consensus

Good morning. Andy Burnham is this morning giving a speech on social care. He is not going to discuss in any detail at all the sort of reform to the system he wants to implement, but instead he will focus on his intention to build a political consensus on the changes needed. He will say:

For decades, governments have kicked this issue down the road because they’ve seen it as too risky, too difficult, and too complicated.

Politicians might have different views but I’m serious about fixing this issue and to do that, we have to find common ground and listen to others to find a way forward.

description:
Committee apologises for not concealing email addresses when alerting witnesses to final report

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Victorian parliamentary committee investigating the harmful impact of cults accidentally sent the email addresses of anonymous survivors who made submissions to current members of such groups and to journalists.

The committee, which had its report into “cults and organised fringe groups” tabled in parliament on Wednesday, emailed hundreds of recipients shortly after midday to inform them it had been published, but erroneously left their addresses visible.

author: Dan Milmo
description:
Energy regulator’s plan would mean upfront fees or financial security via letters of credit, bonds or cash deposits

Datacentre projects in Britain will be forced to put down significant upfront fees to secure an energy connection under proposals to ease an electricity grid logjam.

Ofgem, the sector watchdog, said there were 315 datacentres currently queueing to connect up, representing 73GW of demand. This is almost 30GW above the entire country’s peak energy demand of 45GW.

Continue reading...
title: Datacentre projects could face fees for grid access to ease connection queue, Ofgem says

author: Taz Ali
description:
Emergency workers are continuing their search for survivors in southern Japan after yesterday’s powerful earthquake

  • ‘Race against time’: Japan earthquake death toll rises as rescue teams search for missing

Emergency workers are continuing their search for survivors in southern Japan after yesterday’s powerful earthquake left widespread devastation, with buildings collapsed, roads severely damaged and emergency teams digging through rubble.

At least 13 people have been killed and many reported missing after the earthquake struck the Kumamoto area on the southern main island of Kyushu with a magnitude of 7.1, according to the Japan meteorological agency. The US Geological Survey measured it at magnitude 6.8.
title: Rescue teams face ‘race against time’ in search for trapped survivors as death toll in Japan rises to at least 13 – live updates

author: Sally Weale Education correspondent
description:
PM’s vocational model also takes inspiration from former education secretary Kenneth Baker’s vision

Andy Burnham’s plans to put academic and technical education routes on an equal footing in England have been welcomed by many, but none were more enthusiastic than the former Conservative minister Kenneth Baker.

“I’m very impressed with what he has said,” the 91-year-old former education secretary, home secretary and Conservative party chair told the Guardian. “It’s a very significant announcement. I’m going to try to persuade the Conservative party to support this.”

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham’s plans for technical education build on coalition’s UTC roots

description:
Green party leader says it was ‘a mistake’ and if Farage wants to apologise for times he’s put people in danger, he’ll be happy to say sorry

The Green party leader, Zack Polanski, has said he made an “inadvertent mistake” over a social media image but will not apologise to Nigel Farage.

The image, which Polanski said he “shared inadvertently” on Instagram and then removed, featured a man wearing a black T-shirt with the message “We’re only making plans for Nigel” and an image of a guillotine.

Good morning. Another week, another diplomatic success for Volodymyr Zelenskyy. On Monday, his first meeting with Andy Burnham as PM confirmed continuity in the UK’s steadfast support for Ukraine. “We’ve got your back,” Burnham said as the pair spoke in Portsmouth. Overnight, the US Senate advanced a sweeping Russian sanctions bill.

author: Achol Arok and AAP
description:
Police say search for three-month-old a ‘retrieval effort’ after bodies of mother Helena Wright and toddler found in the ocean near Port Macdonnell

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Hopes of finding a three-month-old boy alive have faded as South Australian police investigate the death of his mother and sister as a murder-suicide.

The bodies of Helena Wright, 36, and her 23-month-old daughter were found in the ocean off the coast west of Port Macdonnell on Monday.

Continue reading...

author: Damien Gayle
description:
Adopting organic free-range model in UK could lead to greenhouse emissions equivalent to 2,316,000 tonnes of CO2, study suggests

Organic eggs are twice as bad for the climate as eggs from chickens living in cages, research suggests.

According to the study, switching the UK’s entire egg production to an organic free-range model would lead to greenhouse gas emissions equivalent to 2,316,000 tonnes of CO2 (tCO2e), while production through a fully caged system would emit 1,184,000 tCO2e.

The latest federal-state stoush on energy comes as S&P Globa

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Former leader shows support for new Victorian premier while paying tribute to Jacinta Allan

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Daniel Andrews has thrown his support behind Victoria’s new premier, Ben Carroll, saying he has what it takes to win November’s state election.

In a rare public statement on Wednesday, the former premier also paid tribute to Jacinta Allan, who he handpicked to replace him as Labor leader when he resigned in September 2023.

description:
ABS data shows inflation still too high but tracking lower than anticipated

Australian mortgage-holders have “dodged a bullet’, with the Reserve Bank now less likely to hike rates next month after new data showed inflation unexpectedly eased to 3.8%, in the year to June, from 4%.

The hotly anticipated consumer price report from the Australian Bureau of Statistics had been seen by some economists as a “make-or-break” moment ahead of the RBA’s upcoming rate decision on 11 August.

description:

Angus Taylor says no payments were made in relation to a growing corruption case involving members of the NSW Liberal party, insisting he is not a party to the proceedings.
